findings.title: Rate card is below the rates in a signed client contract that promises to match any lower rate
findings.quote: Rates apply to change orders and any future SOWs under this Agreement.
findings.explanation: Exhibit A prices three roles below the signed rate card of another AtliQ Inc client for the same roles (the figures are in the exposure section; they are not for a seller). That client's contract says AtliQ warrants its rates are no less favourable than those offered by AtliQ or its Affiliates to any other customer for substantially similar services during the Term, that lower rates must be notified, apply retroactively from the date first offered, and be credited within 30 days; it also gives an annual audit right over this clause. The Term there runs to 31 July 2027, either side can end it on 30 days' notice, and no cap on the credit is stated. Both contracts are with AtliQ Inc, so the 'Affiliates' wording is not needed for the overlap. Whether the two services are 'substantially similar' and whether a rate quoted in a draft counts as 'offered' is a possible conflict, for counsel. Separately, Lakeshore's rates are fixed for 24 months with no increase (§4.2), while the other contract lets AtliQ raise rates 3% a year after month 12, which is also a term in Lakeshore's favour. The tracker says the lower rate was given to win the deal and approved on a call; no date for when it was first offered is in the files.

register_refs.quote: Supplier represents and warrants that the rates, fees and other commercial terms offered to Crestline under this Agreement are and shall remain no less favorable than those offered by Supplier or its Affiliates to any other customer for substantially similar services during the Term.

findings.title: Liability cap of 1x SOW fees, but confidentiality, indemnities and gross negligence sit outside it
findings.quote: EACH PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE UNDER THE APPLICABLE SOW IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM, EXCEPT FOR BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY, INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT.
findings.explanation: The general cap is the SOW fees (USD 64,000 for SOW-1), which matches the checklist of 1x fees. But breach of confidentiality, indemnities and gross negligence or wilful misconduct have no cap, on both sides. Lakeshore Data includes point-of-sale and loyalty data, and the draft refers to personal information in it, so a data incident handled as a confidentiality breach would fall outside the cap. The same carve-outs appear in AtliQ's signed Crestline contract, and in the Kessler Mobility talks Karandeep offered 1x fees 'with carve-outs'. It is bounded by what the carve-outs cover, not unlimited across the board.

register_refs.quote: EXCEPT FOR BREACH OF SECTION 7 OR A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, EACH PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CRESTLINE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM.

findings.title: AtliQ must follow security requirements (Exhibit C) that are not in the file
findings.quote: Vendor shall comply with Lakeshore's Information Security Requirements (Exhibit C) and applicable privacy laws, including the Illinois Personal Information Protection Act.
findings.explanation: Exhibit C is shown only as 'attached separately' and is not in the file. AtliQ would be bound to it, alongside a 72-hour breach notice (§12.2) and the rule that personal information is accessed offshore only in Lakeshore-approved secure environments (§3.2). What Exhibit C requires, for example on where data may be held or who may access it, cannot be tested.

findings.title: Illinois law fits AtliQ Inc, but disputes go to Singapore arbitration
findings.quote: The seat of arbitration shall be Singapore. The tribunal shall consist of one arbitrator. The language of the arbitration shall be English. This forum is selected to align with the dispute resolution framework applicable across the Parent's group of companies.
findings.explanation: The law is Illinois (§13.1), which fits the checklist for AtliQ Inc. The forum is SIAC arbitration seated in Singapore, chosen because of Lakeshore's Singapore parent, for a dispute between two US companies. The Brightwater dispute, also a US entity contract with a foreign forum (English courts), cost USD 14,200 in counsel fees on top of the LD claim; the Singapore seat is a travel and cost question rather than a law question. The register shows AtliQ accepted SIAC at CloudSpan.
